title: Trace-polynomial map between q- and p-degree Artin–Schreier covers
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $q=p^r$ with $r\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with prime subfield $\mathbf F_p$ and field trace $\operatorname{Tr}=\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}:k_0\to\mathbf F_p$ (as in [def-fd-additive-character]), and let $b\in k_0^\times$. Let $X$ be a separated $k_0$-scheme of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Put $\pi_q:Y_q=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)\to X$ and $\pi_{p,b}:Y_{p,b}=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[t]/(t^p-t-bf)\to X$, and let $\sigma_c$ ($c\in k_0$) be the $X$-automorphism of $Y_q$ given by $y\mapsto y+c$ and $\tau_d$ ($d\in\mathbf F_p$) the $X$-automorphism of $Y_{p,b}$ given by $t\mapsto t+d$. Then:

1. $\pi_q$ is finite étale, and on the geometric fibre of $Y_q$ over every geometric point of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] the group $(k_0,+)$ acts simply transitively through $c\mapsto\sigma_c$; in particular every geometric fibre has $q$ points.
2. The additive polynomial $\Theta_b(y)=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(by)^{p^i}$ satisfies $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=b(y^q-y)$ in $\mathcal O_X[y]$, hence $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=bf$ in $\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)$, so $t\mapsto\Theta_b(y)$ defines an $X$-morphism $\theta_b:Y_q\to Y_{p,b}$.
3. $\theta_b\circ\sigma_c=\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}\circ\theta_b$ for every $c\in k_0$.
4. On the geometric fibres over every geometric point of $X$, $\theta_b$ is surjective, and each of its fibres is an orbit, under the $\sigma_c$, of the subgroup $\ker(c\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(bc))$ of order $q/p$.
5. For every morphism $h:X'\to X$ of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with $f'=h^*f$ and $Y'_q$, $Y'_{p,b}$, $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$, $\theta'_b$ formed from $(X',f')$ in the same way, the canonical isomorphisms $Y'_q\cong Y_q\times_XX'$ and $Y'_{p,b}\cong Y_{p,b}\times_XX'$ carry $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$ and $\theta'_b$ to the base changes of $\sigma_c$, $\tau_d$ and $\theta_b$.

proof.text: Empty affine charts contribute empty schemes and can be omitted. On a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the relative-spectrum chart gives $Y_q|_U=\operatorname{Spec}B_q$, $B_q=A[y]/(P_q)$, $P_q=y^q-y-f|_U$, and likewise $B_{p,b}=A[t]/(P_{p,b})$. Localization of these polynomial quotients agrees with quotient after localization on generators, so their algebra sheaves are locally associated to the displayed modules and are quasi-coherent by the cited definition. Both polynomials are monic, of positive degrees $q,p$. The monic-quotient theorem makes $B_q$ finite free with basis $1,y,\ldots,y^{q-1}$. Since $q=p^r$ and $p=0$ in $A$, $P_q^\prime=-1$. The standard-étale theorem identifies $A[y]_{P_q^\prime}/(P_q)$ with $B_q$ (localizing at $-1$ changes nothing) and proves its spectrum étale over $U$. Thus $\pi_q$ is finite by the affine-chart definition, and étale by the affine-local characterization in the cited definition. The same argument also applies to $\pi_{p,b}$.

For any $h:X^\prime\to X$, apply relative-Spec base change to the two quotient algebra sheaves. Locally a ring map $A\to A^\prime$ sends $f$ to $f^\prime$. For affine opens $U^\prime\subseteq h^{-1}(U)$, the affine-sections theorem for pullbacks identifies the sections of $h^*$ of each quotient algebra sheaf over $U^\prime$ with $A^\prime\otimes_A$ its sections over $U$, by $s\otimes a^\prime\mapsto a^\prime h^*s$; this map is multiplicative on such simple tensors. There is an isomorphism $$A^\prime\otimes_A A[y]/(y^q-y-f)\;\cong\; A^\prime[y]/(y^q-y-f^\prime).$$ It sends $a^\prime\otimes y$ to $a^\prime y$. Its inverse sends $a^\prime$ to $a^\prime\otimes1$ and $y$ to $1\otimes y$; the relation is zero on both sides. These maps are inverse on the coefficient ring and generator, hence on the whole algebra. The same maps with $t$ and $bf$ give the prime-degree version. These formulas commute with restrictions and supply the canonical identifications $Y_q^\prime\cong Y_q\times_X X^\prime$ and $Y_{p,b}^\prime\cong Y_{p,b}\times_X X^\prime$. This also identifies a geometric fibre with the same quotient over its algebraically closed residue field.

proof.text: Frobenius is additive, and $c^q=c$ for $c\in k_0$. Consequently $(y+c)^q-(y+c)-f=y^q-y-f$. Substitution $y\mapsto y+c$ defines a quotient algebra automorphism, with inverse $y\mapsto y-c$. The substitutions respect restrictions, so the relative-Spec anti-equivalence gives $\sigma_c$ globally. Their compositions obey $\sigma_c\sigma_e=\sigma_{c+e}$. The identical calculation using $d^p=d$ gives $\tau_d$ on $Y_{p,b}$. No assertion about the full automorphism group of a disconnected cover is needed.

source.place: Tag 00UB polynomial presentation; explicit substitutions and inverses (agent calculation).

proof.text: Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be geometric and $a=f(\bar x)$. By step 2 its $q$-cover fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[y]/(y^q-y-a)$. The derivative is $-1$; the Bézout identity $0\cdot P+(-1)P^\prime=1$ proves separability. The cited root theorem, with $F=\Omega$ and the identity embedding into $\Omega$, gives $q$ distinct roots. The root theorem also factors $P$ as the product of $y-\rho$ over those roots. Every prime ideal of the quotient contains one factor, so is $(y-\rho)$, with residue field $\Omega$. Thus its points and geometric points are exactly these roots. For a chosen root $\alpha$, the $q$ distinct values $\alpha+c$ ($c\in k_0$) are roots by step 3; they exhaust the root set. Translation is therefore simply transitive. The same reasoning for $t^p-t-ba$ gives its $p$ distinct roots, a simply transitive $\mathbf F_p$-set. This proves clause 1.

source.place: Tag 01LX geometric base-change chart; separability and the root count are the cited polynomial statements.

proof.text: In every $k_0$-algebra of sections, Frobenius gives $$\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}(by)^{p^i}-\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(by)^{p^i}=(by)^{p^r}-by=b(y^q-y),$$ where the last equality uses $b^q=b$. This is an identity already in $\mathcal O_X[y]$. Reducing modulo $y^q-y-f$ gives $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=bf$. Therefore the algebra map on each affine chart fixing coefficients and sending $t$ to $\Theta_b(y)$ factors through $B_{p,b}\to B_q$. The formulas agree on restrictions, hence define a map of the quotient algebra sheaves. The relative-Spec anti-equivalence supplies the claimed $X$-morphism $\theta_b$. This proves clause 2.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140, Lang torsor and pullback; explicit trace-polynomial realization and telescoping calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: The new trace-formula leaf with $K=\mathbf F_p$, $L=k_0$ gives $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(bc)^{p^i}=\operatorname{Tr}(bc)$ in $k_0$. Here $[k_0:\mathbf F_p]=r$: a basis of size $n$ identifies its underlying set with $\mathbf F_p^n$, so $p^n=q=p^r$ implies $n=r$. Additivity of the Frobenius iterates now gives $$\Theta_b(y+c)=\Theta_b(y)+\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(bc)^{p^i}=\Theta_b(y)+\operatorname{Tr}(bc).$$ On coordinate algebras the two composites in clause 3 fix all coefficients and send $t$ to the two equal displayed expressions. Faithfulness of the relative-Spec anti-equivalence gives $\theta_b\circ\sigma_c=\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}\circ\theta_b$ globally.

source.place: (1.1.3), Lang torsor pushout; explicit equivariance calculation using Mathlib/FieldTheory/Finite/Trace.lean:49–56.

proof.text:
Put $T_b(c)=\operatorname{Tr}(bc)$. The polynomial expression from step 6 and Frobenius additivity show $T_b$ additive. For $d\in\mathbf F_p$, $d^{p^i}=d$ by the finite-field power identity, so $T_b(dc)=dT_b(c)$. Since $b
e0$, trace-pairing nondegeneracy supplies $c_0$ with $e=T_b(c_0)
e0$. Each $d\in\mathbf F_p$ has preimage $(d/e)c_0$, proving surjectivity. If $c_d$ is a preimage of $d$, the map $u\mapsto c_d+u$ is a bijection $\ker T_b	o T_b^{-1}(d)$ with inverse $c\mapsto c-c_d$. These $p$ fibres partition the $q$-element set $k_0$, hence $\#\ker T_b=q/p$. This argument does not use $\operatorname{Tr}(1)
e0$, which fails when $p$ divides $r$.

source.place: (0.2), p. 135, finite-field trace character; nondegeneracy from the existing Mathlib leaf, followed by the explicit linear and coset calculations.

proof.text: On a geometric fibre choose $\alpha$ in the $q$-cover as in step 4 and set $\beta=\Theta_b(\alpha)$, a root of $t^p-t-ba$ by step 5. Every point of the target fibre is uniquely $\beta+d$, $d\in\mathbf F_p$. By step 6, $\theta_b(\alpha+c)=\beta+T_b(c)$. The surjectivity from step 7 therefore lifts every target point. Two source points $\alpha+c$ and $\alpha+c^\prime$ have the same image exactly when $T_b(c^\prime-c)=0$. Their difference belongs to $\ker T_b$ exactly in this case, which says that every fibre is a single orbit of that subgroup under the translations. Its order is $q/p$ by step 7. This proves clause 4.

source.place: (1.1.3), pushout of a Lang torsor; explicit calculation on the two geometric torsor fibres.

proof.text: It remains to check the maps in clause 5 under the canonical cover identifications of step 2. On a chart with coefficient map $\varphi:A\to A^\prime$, every $k_0$-constant is fixed and $\varphi(f)=f^\prime$. Thus the base-changed substitutions for $\sigma_c$ and $\tau_d$ are literally $y\mapsto y+c$ and $t\mapsto t+d$. For the third map, $$\varphi\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}b^{p^i}y^{p^i}\right)=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}b^{p^i}y^{p^i}$$ in $A^\prime[y]$, which is the polynomial defining $\theta_b^\prime$. These equalities on the coefficient ring and coordinate generator give equality of the quotient algebra maps. By the naturality clause of the affine-sections theorem for pullbacks, the pullbacks of the substitution maps become $\varphi$-tensored substitutions under those identifications. They commute with restriction, so the affine-morphism anti-equivalence and the canonical relative-Spec base-change isomorphisms identify the global maps too. This proves clause 5 for every stated $h$; the algebra calculation requires no flatness.
